extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, educators, academic administrators, and technical professionals (early 20th-century UK/Empire context)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the standards and selection criteria discussed on the page around recognition of full‑time teaching service, associated evidence requirements, and related appointment/book‑evaluation criteria. Covers what counts as teaching service, required documentary evidence, and examples of selection criteria for academic posts and for judging technical/scientific books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal agreement as evidence of full-time teaching service
rubrics_metrics.description: The first essential for recognition of full-time teaching service should be a formal agreement between employer and teacher in which should be clearly set out the nature of the duties, whether they are wholly of a teaching character, the extent of the employer’s claim upon the teacher’s working hours, and the restrictions, if any, put upon the employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an agreement ought to be sufficient evidence (the editor argues it would be sufficient for a judge or jury and for ordinary head/assistant teachers). However, the Board indicates it may still require additional information for some categories (see technical teachers). Include clear specification of duties, hours, restrictions, and status in the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component definition of full-time teaching service
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-time teaching service consists essentially of two component parts: actual teaching before a class, and the subsidiary duties entailed by actual teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proportional value of these components depends upon the subject taught, the standard reached, the technicality of the subject, and experimental preparation involved. Any assessment must consider both direct teaching hours and time spent on subsidiary activities tied to teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for documentary evidence for technical/college teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: For specialist teachers and teachers in technical schools and colleges, it will be necessary to call for information as to the actual teaching hours as evidence of their full-time employment; an approved agreement may not be accepted as sufficient evidence by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because subsidiary duties vary widely in technical subjects, the Board may demand more than a mere return of actual teaching hours—i.e., additional information about preparation, supervision, and other duties—so institutions should supply detailed accounts of teaching-related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson preparation and professional updating counted as subsidiary duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific preparation of lessons (as distinct from general study) is regarded as a subsidiary duty entailed by actual teaching; time spent by teachers of science and technology in keeping in touch with modern developments is not 'general study' dissociated from teaching and should be regarded as part of teaching service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should recognise that technical subjects require substantial ongoing professional updating and experimental preparation (e.g., electrical engineering vs. Roman history). Such time is essential and should be counted when determining full-time status and pensionable service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of research work relative to teaching service (Board's clause 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular indicates (clause 7) that research work will not be regarded as teaching service, and time spent in research work would not be counted as teaching service for the purpose of the Superannuation Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion is contested in the review: distinguish between (a) research undertaken for outside firms and remunerated as private work (reasonably excluded) and (b) research intrinsic to institutional teaching—especially supervising student research—which the reviewer argues should count as pensionable teaching service. Policies should state how institution-based research and supervision are classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for Lecturer in Mechanical Engineering (University of Hong Kong)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be graduates in Engineering of some British University; preference given to unmarried men; require a sound knowledge of workshop practice, ability to take students in steam and oil engine work and to lecture on practical subjects; expected to keep all plant of the laboratories in running order; appointment on five years' agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary and terms specified (salary £450 per annum, conversion/allowances, free quarters or £100 allowance, half salary from date of embarkation). Applications to be submitted in covers marked 'C.A.' to the Secretary, Board of Education, with stated deadlines. These explicit conditions form the hiring rubric for the post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for Assistant Master (Sandown County Secondary School)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be graduates, preferably in Honours, and should state what subsidiary subjects they can offer; willingness to take part in out-of-school activities will be a strong recommendation; salary paid according to the Burnham Secondary scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications require further particulars and forms; willingness to contribute to extra-curricular life is an explicit positive evaluation factor for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment conditions for University of Manchester bacteriology posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Lecturer in Bacteriology (stipend £500 p.a.) and Demonstrator in Bacteriology (stipend £400 p.a.); appointees must join the Federated Superannuation System for Universities; a medical qualification is not an essential condition of either appointment; applications should be accompanied by three testimonials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipend levels, pension system membership, testimonial requirements and the non-essential nature of a medical qualification constitute selection/appointment criteria for these academic posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluating scientific books (Internal Secretion review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful books are judged by their object and scope, readability for intended audience, scientific presentation of known facts, value as reference works, and caution against sensationalism; inclusion of indexes and bibliographies is important for reference value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish popular presentations (accessible, readable) from works of reference (comprehensive, detailed). A good bibliography (especially indicating important original works) and a good index increase a book's utility for research workers and teachers. Avoid loose or misleading terminology; prefer precise definitions and careful phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for balancing textbook and reference work (Reservoir and Other Dams review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A work that attempts to be both a compact textbook and an exhaustive reference may fail both aims; desirable features of a standard authority include comprehensive diagrams, particulars of notable examples, recent updates (new chapters on crest gates and spillways), appendices with specifications, bibliography and a full index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For students prefer portable, concise texts; for practitioners prefer exhaustive reference material with detailed plates and case examples. Bibliography should be well organised (alphabetical) to facilitate tracing sources. Inclusion of up-to-date notable examples and technical appendices increases practitioner value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for assessing legal/technical books on patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful treatment links procedures for obtaining a patent, establishing validity in courts (interpretation and grounds of invalidity), and the privileges/responsibilities of patentees (infringement, royalties, licences, liabilities). Clarity and concise avoidance of undue legal technicalities widen readership to business and industrial research directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable appendices consolidate statutes and leading cases; inclusion of forms and rules may be less valuable relative to consolidated acts and case lists. Presentation sequence that links principles coherently is judged favourably.
